summary: Shimei Futabatei was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied at Senshu College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and Hitotsubashi University. He taught at the Army War College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and Naval War College.

Shin Fujinaga works in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 1992) and as an associate professor at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested 2000).

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a doctorate at Kyoto University, studying under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami. He served as a professor at Hanazono University, Ryukoku University, and Kyoto University.

Shin'ichi Tsuda is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and earned his Ph.D. at Australian National University under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham, later teaching at ICPBS (~1996-2008).

Shin'ichi Yoshinaga was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He later served as a professor at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College (attested 2015).
Shindai Sekiguchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1928-1934). He later served as a professor at Taisho University (~1957-1977) and Hanazono University (~1977-1982).

Shindo Kusumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under the supervision of Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

Shingen Takagi was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at Tohoku University and Rissho University (PhD), studying under Kanakura, Hadano, Nakano, and Miyasaka. He served as associate professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991-1995) at Koyasan University.

Shingo Einoo is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He worked at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1986-1989) and the University of Tokyo (~1989-2013).

Shinichi Nakazawa is a scholar in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1969-1977). He held posts at Chuo University (~1993-2006), Tama Art University (~2006-2011), and Meiji University (~2011-2020).
Shinjiro Kazama is a linguistics scholar who studied at Hokkaido University (~1984-1993). He held posts at Tottori University (~1995-2001) and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (professor, ~2009).

Shinjo Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Hajime Nakamura and Dale Maurice Riepe, attending Columbia University. He taught as a Fulbright lecturer at University at Buffalo and served as professor at the University of Tsukuba (1975-1997).

Shinjo Mochizuki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He was educated at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo (~1920-1923), and later held a post at Tezukayama Gakuin University.

Shinjo Suguro was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held posts as professor (~1970-1996) and emeritus professor (~1996-2002) at Rissho University, and served as deputy director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra (1980).

Shinkai Sugawara was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Waseda University and received a doctorate from Taisho University. He served on the faculty at Waseda University (~1966-1996), where he became professor emeritus.

Shinkan Murakami is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his doctorate at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Ryujo Yamada, and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as professor (~1974-1996) and professor emeritus at Tohoku University.

Shinko Mochizuki was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Bukkyo, Taisho, and Tokyo universities. He served as professor and president of Taisho University across multiple terms between 1914 and 1942, and held a post at Chion-in Temple (~1946-1948).

Shinko Nakai was a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Kyoto Prefectural University (~1962-1966). He later served as university president and professor emeritus at Bukkyo University (~1977-2014).

Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey (attested 2003), teacher Mark Csikszentmihalyi (2000), and academic adviser Robert Bickner.
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned a PhD at Nagoya University (-1995). Yamaguchi held an appointment as a professor at Toyo University (attested 2015).
